conceptZh: 爸爸的爸爸，或對年長男性的敬稱。
object: a top-hat magician rabbit, an oversized white fake mustache, and a gentle toy grandpa walrus
morph: a giant fake mustache and tiny rabbit swap sizes while 公 forms from a magic hat
creativeAngle: 魔術兔把鬍子變太大，被壓到小小的；最後變出老爺爺玩偶對應「阿公」。
promptEn: An 8-second silly animated clip, bright pastel look, soft daylight, no dark grading. On a plum-and-gold toy stage with a spangled curtain, a magician rabbit in a tilted top hat taps his wand over an empty hat, ready for a trick that will go wrong. 0–1.7s: With the first 公 spoken, he waves the wand and an enormous white mustache bursts out of the hat, larger than the rabbit, flopping over his whole face. 1.7–3.4s: Stuck under the mustache, he improvises: the second 公 is spoken as he ties the mustache into a big bow and rides it like a sled across the stage, ears streaming. 3.4–5.0s: Wand tap again: the mustache shrinks to a speck, and out of the hat tumble two jaunty ink-red stroke pieces that click into the glyph 公 in the middle of the stage. 5.0–5.9s: As 阿公 is spoken, a kindly toy walrus grandpa with spectacles pops from the hat, wearing the tiny mustache, and the rabbit bows, startled but delighted. Final hold (about 5.0–8.0s): the walrus grandpa tips his cap and the rabbit pulls a daisy from his sleeve, both well away from the strokes. Voice: a friendly unseen narrator speaks, in Taiwanese Mandarin and at an unhurried pace, precisely these syllables and then falls silent: 公、公、阿公（ㄍㄨㄥ、ㄍㄨㄥ、ㄚ ㄍㄨㄥ）. The first 公 lands at about 0.9s, the second 公 at about 2.7s, and the word 阿公 at about 5.0s, each timed to the picture described above. The only text anywhere in frame is the single glyph 公, drawn in one saturated solid color on a much lighter pastel backdrop; no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no logos. The glyph 公 fills roughly 70% of frame height, centered and uncropped, and stays perfectly still for the final 3 seconds while the lead keeps playing away from the strokes. No real people, no flashing.

meaning: grandfather; respectful term for an older man
conceptZh: 爸爸的爸爸叫阿公；也用來尊稱年紀大的男性。
object: a squeaky pull-back toy race car with googly eyes stacking four ink-red foam pieces (two short slanted bars, one bent elbow piece, one round dot) into a wobbling tower to reach a cookie jar on a high shelf
morph: the car crashes nose-first into its own tower with every delivery; the bouncy astronaut drifts down and sits on top as the one piece too many; the tower topples and the four red pieces land flat as the strokes of 公: the two slanted bars as the top 八 pair, the elbow piece as the 撇折 and the dot as the final 點, while the car is buried with only its googly eyes showing
creativeAngle: 前一版是兔子魔術師的鬍子戲法，這次完全換成「疊高高再垮掉」的實體笑料：賽車每送一塊都衝過頭、鼻子先撞，塔越疊越歪；太空人在最糟的時刻飄下來當最後一塊，停一拍，整座塔嘩啦垮成 公。四塊泡棉與四筆一一對應（八兩斜筆＋ㄙ的折筆和點），說「阿公」時太空人從堆裡冒出來，戴著摔下來的眼鏡和棉花鬍子、拄著小拐杖，畫面就是阿公的樣子，聲音與畫面同一個故事。
promptEn:
An 8-second slapstick animated clip in a bright pastel toy-room look, soft even daylight, no dark grading, nothing busy behind. Lead: a squeaky pull-back toy race car with big googly eyes, a cheerful show-off that always overshoots and crashes nose first. Goal: a cookie jar on a high shelf at the top of frame. Props: four chunky ink-red foam pieces lying on the floor, two short slanted bars, one bent elbow piece and one round dot. Buddy: a bouncy astronaut toy in a fishbowl helmet who keeps floating off the ground at the wrong moment.

0–1.5s: The car stares up at the cookie jar, googly eyes rattling, pulls itself back with a loud squeak and launches. It shoves the first red bar upright under the shelf, skids past it, bonks the wall nose first and bounces back with a dizzy grin. The first 公 is spoken at about 0.8s, right as that first piece thumps into place and the build begins.

1.5–3.3s: Faster now. The car rears up on its back wheels like tiptoe, balancing the second bar and then the elbow piece on top, each delivery a pull-back dash that overshoots, so the car clips the tower nose first and the stack sways wider and wider, leaning left, leaning right, the car wobbling underneath with its eyes spinning.

3.3–4.6s: The astronaut drifts in from the side, feet off the floor, bobbing like a balloon, and plops down on the very top of the swaying tower as the one piece too many. Everything freezes for a half-second beat: car, astronaut, tower all holding their breath. Then the whole stack tips and comes down in a tumbling, squashy heap.

4.6–5.4s: The pieces land with soft foam thumps and lie flat as the glyph 公 in the center of the frame: the two slanted bars settle as the top 八 pair, the elbow piece as the bent lower stroke and the round dot as the final small stroke on the right. The second 公 is spoken at about 4.7s, exactly as the last piece lands and the glyph is complete. The car is buried under a soft heap of fallen cushions in the lower-left corner, well outside the strokes, with only its two googly eyes poking out and blinking.

5.4–8.0s: The glyph 公 stays perfectly still and readable. At about 5.8s the word 阿公 is spoken, and at that same moment the astronaut pops up from the cushions at the lower right, outside the strokes, now wearing a pair of round toy spectacles and a puff of white cotton-wool beard that fell with the stack, leaning on a tiny bent-foam cane and giving a slow, kindly grandpa wave. The car's googly eyes swivel toward him and bounce with delight; the astronaut floats up a few centimeters and gently bonks the underside of the shelf, so the cookie jar wobbles but stays put. Nobody touches or covers the strokes.

Voice: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, slow and distinct with clear tones, reads exactly these syllables and then falls silent: 公、公、阿公（ㄍㄨㄥ、ㄍㄨㄥ、ㄚ ㄍㄨㄥ）. No other dialogue, no explanation, no translation, no repeated chanting. Only soft squeaks, foam thumps and a quiet gentle background tune well under the voice; no loud startling sounds.

The only text anywhere in frame is the single glyph 公, correctly formed in one saturated solid red against the much lighter pastel floor, centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with clear margins. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no logos, no watermark, no flashing effects. No real people and no realistic human figures; the astronaut is unmistakably a toy with a round plastic fishbowl helmet. Final clear hold of the finished glyph for the last 3 seconds while the car and astronaut keep playing away from the strokes.

meaning: grandfather; also a respectful word for an older man
conceptZh: 短手臂的橡膠恐龍搆不到躲在四根紅色保齡球瓶後面的調皮小老鼠，於是退到最遠處助跑、肚子貼地滑過亮晶晶的地板，一記全倒把球瓶撞飛，翻滾落地拼成「公」，一撮白棉花鬍子剛好掉在恐龍鼻子上，讓牠變成笑咪咪的阿公。
object: a squeaky green rubber dinosaur with enormous feet and comically tiny arms, a tiny cheeky cartoon mouse, four chunky ink-red foam bowling pins (two straight, one bendy, one short round), and a fluffy white cotton mustache prop
morph: a belly-slide strike sends the four red pins spinning; the two straight pins land as the top left-falling and right-falling strokes, the bendy pin folds into the lower bent stroke, and the short round pin rolls into the final dot, forming 公
creativeAngle: 早期版本是安靜的搖椅爺爺、魔術兔和推疊積木的賽車，這次換成肚子貼地滑行的保齡球全倒：恐龍手太短搆不到，只好用整個身體當保齡球，撞擊本身就把四根球瓶撞成「公」的四筆。「阿公」這個詞由白棉花鬍子落在恐龍鼻子上、恐龍駝背扮爺爺來呈現，聽到的和看到的是同一個畫面。
promptEn:
An 8-second slapstick animated clip, bright pastel toy-room look, soft even daylight, no dark grading, a plain shiny cream floor and nothing busy behind. Lead: a squeaky green rubber dinosaur with enormous floppy feet and comically tiny arms that never reach anything, stubborn and proud, so it uses its whole body instead. Rival: a tiny original cartoon mouse with big round ears, lightning fast and always grinning. Props: four chunky ink-red foam bowling pins standing in a row at center right (two tall straight pins, one bendy pin, one short round pin). On top of the round pin sits a fluffy white cotton mustache.

0–1.6s: The mouse peeks out from behind the pins and waves a cookie. The dinosaur stomps up and stretches its tiny arms toward it, straining and wiggling its fingers, but they stop a centimeter short. The mouse nibbles the cookie and grins. The first 公 is spoken at about 0.9s as the dino starts to strain.

1.6–3.2s: The dinosaur huffs, waddles backward all the way to the far left edge, paws the floor with one huge foot, then charges THUMP-THUMP-THUMP and dives onto its round belly, sliding across the shiny floor like a bowling ball, eyes wide and tail streaming.

3.2–4.4s: STRIKE. It smacks into the row and the pins burst upward, spinning in cartoon arcs. The mouse is flipped up too, giggling as it flies, and the white mustache flutters away.

4.4–5.0s: The pins thump down flat into the glyph 公, centered: the two straight pins land as the top pair of strokes, one slanting down-left and one slanting down-right; the bendy pin folds into the lower bent stroke; the round pin rolls into place as the small final dot. The second 公 is spoken at about 4.6s as the last pin settles. The mouse lands safely on the lower right, outside the strokes.

5.0–8.0s: The dinosaur pops up at the lower left in a strike pose, tiny arms raised high. At about 5.6s the word 阿公 is spoken just as the white mustache drops onto its snout; it hunches over like a kindly grandpa and taps its tail on the floor like a cane, while the mouse claps and bounces. Both stay clear of the strokes. The glyph 公 stays perfectly still for the final 3 seconds.

Voice: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, slowly and distinctly with clear tones, reads exactly these syllables, then falls silent: 公、公、阿公 (ㄍㄨㄥ、ㄍㄨㄥ、ㄚ ㄍㄨㄥ). No other speech. There are only soft squeaks, foam thumps and a quiet tune well under the voice.

The only text in frame is the single correctly formed glyph 公, in solid saturated red on the much lighter floor. It is centered, uncropped and fills about 70% of frame height with clear margins. No subtitles, no other text, no logos, no watermark, no flashing. All characters are clearly cartoon toys.
